name: Perforate st John's-wort
grown_as: A wild perennial of grassland, banks and waste ground.
habit: An upright perennial 30 to 80 cm (up to 1 m), stiff stems branching in the upper part, with a broad, flat-topped spread of golden flowers. Spreads by short creeping runners at the base.

leaf.arrangement: Opposite pairs, stalkless; the stem round with two thin raised lines running down it, one each side between the leaf pairs
leaf.outline: Oblong to narrowly oval, 1 to 3 cm long
leaf.margin: Smooth, untoothed, with a few tiny black dots on the edge underneath
leaf.veins: A midrib and a few faint side veins
leaf.surface: Hairless. Held up to the light it is peppered with many tiny clear dots like pinpricks (the 'perforations')

flower.form: A flat, open, five-pointed star with a fluffy centre
flower.petals: Five, free, oval and a little lopsided, with tiny black dots along the edges
flower.centre: A burst of many long yellow stamens in three bundles around three styles, giving a fluffy look
flower.behind: Five narrow, pointed green sepals, showing a little between the petals
flower.carried: Many together in branched, broad, flat-topped to rounded clusters at the tops of the stems, facing up

fruit: Egg-shaped, pointed capsules about 6 to 8 mm, with three styles at the tip, ripening reddish brown in the branched head; the dead stems stand brown into winter. Seeds tiny (about 1 mm), cylindrical, dark brown, finely pitted.
seedling: Two tiny oval seed leaves, then opposite pairs of small oval leaves
winter: Low leafy shoots and runners at the base, often reddish, with the old brown flower stems standing above.

leaf: small oblong stalkless leaf, untoothed, blunt
many tiny clear dots in the leaf
bloom: five golden yellow petals in a star
a fluffy burst of many long stamens
tiny black dots on the petal edges
seedling: first true leaves small opposite ovals
young: upright stems with opposite pairs of small oblong leaves
flower: stiff upright stems branching at the top
broad flat-topped clusters of golden star flowers
seedhead: branched heads of pointed reddish-brown capsules on stiff stems
dormant: low leafy shoots at the base with old brown stems above

look_alikes: Imperforate St John's-wort (Hypericum maculatum) has a square stem with four raised lines and few or no clear dots. Square-stalked St John's-wort (H. tetrapterum) has winged square stems and smaller paler flowers. Hairy St John's-wort is downy. Ragwort has daisy flowers and cut leaves.
